builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Maximising Transparency in Context Compaction Improves Retention of Facts and Commitments for Lightweight Coding Agents
summary: It replaces model-written summary compaction (and rewording-based deterministic compaction) with a deterministic scheme that keeps user and assistant prose verbatim and explicitly flags where information was stripped. Cost is low in complexity and compute, but retaining verbatim text preserves less aggressively than summarization, so effective context capacity may be tighter and no extra latency figures are given. It can fail when verbatim retention crowds out needed context under heavy compaction, and the evidence rests on the authors' own benchmarks tied to the Pi coding agent, so transfer to other agents and workloads is unverified.
rationale: The method is cheap, deterministic, and targets exactly the lightweight-model regime the reader operates in, but the single-agent implementation and absence of quantified gains require validation on the reader's own workloads before production adoption.
technique: Transparent deterministic context compaction with verbatim prose retention

claims.statement: It replaces model-written summary compaction (and rewording-based deterministic compaction) with a deterministic scheme that keeps user and assistant prose verbatim and explicitly flags where information was stripped. Cost is low in complexity and compute, but retaining verbatim text preserves less aggressively than summarization, so effective context capacity may be tighter and no extra latency figures are given. It can fail when verbatim retention crowds out needed context under heavy compaction, and the evidence rests on the authors' own benchmarks tied to the Pi coding agent, so transfer to other agents and workloads is unverified.

On commitment and fact-recall benchmarks, transparent-compact matched or outperformed model-written summarization and the deterministic pi-vcc method across four models, with the largest advantage for the lightweight Qwen3.8-27B in avoiding confident blunders; the advantage persisted but shrank with a frontier model. No quantitative magnitude is reported.
